findings.explanation: 1 cookie(s) classified as requiring consent were stored before any interaction with the page: _ga (Google Analytics, analytics, first-party). Art. 5(3) requires prior consent for storing information on the visitor's device unless it is strictly necessary for a service the visitor requested.
No request to a known analytics or advertising service, and no unclassified beacon-like request, was observed before any interaction. No third-party site was contacted.
No localStorage or sessionStorage key associated with analytics or advertising was written before any interaction. No Web Storage key was written.
A consent interface was detected on the page (unidentified platform; controls recognised: accept, close).

Possible issue, from a low-confidence signal; please verify. The first layer of the consent interface offers acceptance (“J’accepte”) but no refusal option was found; other controls: “×” (close). The CNIL strongly recommends that refusing be possible on the same screen and as easily as accepting, and most authorities in the EDPB Cookie Banner Taskforce considered a banner with no refusal option on any layer to be an infringement.
The analytics cookie(s) stored before consent have a lifetime of 13 months or less: _ga (12.0 months (365 days)).
This point cannot be established by observing the website from outside. It is listed so a reviewer can examine it.
